findings.anchor: export function fetchUser(id: string, timeoutMs: number): [Record<string, unknown>, number] {
findings.body: The timeoutMs parameter previously defaulted to 30_000 but now has no default, requiring every caller to supply a value explicitly. If any caller omits it (e.g. via untyped JS interop) timeoutMs could be undefined, effectively disabling any timeout enforcement downstream.
findings.failure_scenario: If a caller invokes fetchUser without a timeoutMs (possible from JS callers not type-checked), the value becomes undefined and any downstream logic using it as a timeout could hang indefinitely, causing a resource exhaustion/DoS risk.
findings.title: Removed default timeout value may cause unbounded/undefined timeout

findings.anchor: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toGMTString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.body: Date.prototype.toGMTString is a deprecated legacy alias retained only for compatibility; toISOString (or toUTCString) is the standard modern replacement.
findings.failure_scenario: toGMTString remains functional in current engines but is marked deprecated in the spec and could be removed or flagged by linters/future runtimes, and its non-ISO output format differs from the original code's ISO string, potentially breaking downstream consumers expecting ISO-8601 formatted timestamps.
findings.suggestion: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toISOString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.title: Replace deprecated toGMTString with toISOString
